headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Plane can expose files/notes while the RAG course agent reads/writes local files and secrets in a shared development environment.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can handle file uploads and hyperlinks, while the course agent reads files and processes notebook/API inputs in a local development environment. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Plane outputs are copied into the RAG workflow. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Plane outputs are pasted into the course agent's prompts or notebooks, injected instructions can be followed.
IF a shared folder is used to move Plane exports into the RAG course workspace, file content can become prompt content.
mitigations: Keep Plane exports out of prompts; paste only sanitized excerpts.
Use a separate folder for imported artifacts and mark it read-only.
Add a one-line instruction filter before any pasted content.
Review any file-uploaded content before feeding it to the course agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported documents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps, and the course agent reads files, handles configuration secrets, and writes files in a local development environment. If they share a workspace, Plane content can flow into the course agent's context and then into external APIs or logs. The shared-workspace path is not explicitly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at high rather than critical.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory tree, Plane files can be read by the course agent.
IF the course agent sends retrieved context to its APIs, shared files may leave the local environment.
IF secrets are present in the shared workspace, they can be exposed through notebook or API traces.
mitigations: Store Plane data in a separate workspace.
Remove secrets from any shared directory immediately.
Disable file ingestion for the course agent when processing Plane exports.
Rotate any secrets that may have been copied into notebooks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane has no filesystem write, while the course agent can read and write files and spawn subprocesses. They can still contend over shared local artifacts if run in the same development tree, but the lack of Plane write capability and no git modification on the course agent reduces direct conflict severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, the course agent can overwrite Plane-exported artifacts.
IF the operator uses a shared checkout for notebooks and Plane data, file contention can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Mount Plane data read-only for the course agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane produces issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and hyperlinks, and the course agent is an agentic RAG system with ask/stream endpoints that can act on retrieved content. If Plane output is treated as authoritative input, the course agent can propagate mistakes into generated answers or downstream actions. No built-in verification bridge is documented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Plane-generated text is fed into the course agent's retrieval corpus, the agent may treat it as ground truth.
IF the course agent's outputs are used operationally, any mistaken Plane content can cascade into user-visible actions.
mitigations: Require human review of Plane-derived facts before ingestion.
Tag Plane content as untrusted in the RAG index.
Limit the course agent to citation-only answers for imported content.
Sample-check generated outputs against source files.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane is self-hostable and touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and notes, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment. The pair can therefore create retention and residency mismatches if Plane data or secrets are copied into notebooks or API logs. No explicit compliance controls are documented for either agent, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane data is exported into the course agent's notebooks, retention policies may diverge.
IF secrets or personal data are stored in shared logs, deletion requests may not reach both systems.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the course agent workspace.
Document retention for Plane exports and notebook outputs.
Delete copied artifacts after each run.
Restrict logs from containing secrets or personal data.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
